subject.title: fix: harden recovered meeting browser sessions

question: Should recovered talk-back sessions fail closed whenever `micMuted` is unknown, and what proof is required before accepting that compatibility change?
rationale: The earlier extraction preserved unknown microphone state as ready and described it as shipped behavior, while this PR intentionally trades possible recovery stalls for protection against silently dropped speech; tests cannot choose that product contract.

options.title: Approve strict readiness with live proof
options.body: Require explicit `micMuted: false`, add redacted live Google Meet recovery and speech evidence, then merge after exact-head checks pass.

options.title: Approve a proof override
options.body: Accept the strict contract based on deterministic regression coverage and record an explicit maintainer override because a controlled two-party meeting is impractical.

options.title: Preserve unknown-state compatibility
options.body: Keep unknown microphone state ready until every talk-back adapter reliably reports microphone status, avoiding upgrade stalls while retaining the silent-speech risk.

recommendation.title: Approve strict readiness with live proof
recommendation.body: Require explicit `micMuted: false`, add redacted live Google Meet recovery and speech evidence, then merge after exact-head checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the shared meeting runtime, documented this deferred policy choice, and own the current follow-up implementation.
